title: Where does the compass go to draw an eye?
description: A painted mask opens the video. Its eyes are made of two arcs that meet at two corners, and the video stops on the question of where the two arc centres must go.
teaching_notes: One idea: each arc of an eye needs a centre, and guessing gives a lopsided eye. Watch for students who say the centres can simply be placed by eye; do not confirm any guess, because the next topic finds the centres exactly.

video_script.why: Before any construction, the child meets the real question: where exactly the two centres of an eye's arcs must be so that the upper and lower arcs match.
video_script.substitution: Picture each arc of the eye as part of a circle, drawn with the compass point at a hidden centre.
video_script.anchor: Two arcs make an eye: where must the compass point go for each arc?
never_show: the arcs from X and Y meeting at the centres
the line through the two centres
maths_rules: An eye is two arcs that meet at two corners X and Y.
Each arc is part of a circle with its own centre; the lower arc's centre lies above XY and the upper arc's centre lies below XY.
For an even eye, the two arcs have the same radius.
The open question is where the two centres go. The answer is never shown or hinted.
video_script.design: One idea: an eye needs two exact centres. Assumes the child can draw an arc with a compass. The photo sits as a dimmed backdrop in the first beat and fades before the drawn eye arrives; the eye stays to the end.
